title: Isomorphism lifting from directed Hom continuity
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, C_k categories, F_k(b) objects for b in {false,true}, D a category, O(b) objects of D, G_k:C_k→D functors and ψ_k(b):G_k(F_k(b))≅O(b). A DirectedPerfectHomSystem means transport of all four kinds of Hom sets along k≤l preserves identity and composition, preserves the conjugated limit map ψ_k(a)^{-1}G_k(f)ψ_k(b), every limit morphism lifts at a stage, and equal limit images of two stage maps imply equality of their transports at every stage beyond some later index. For every e:O(false)≅O(true), there exist k and e_k:F_k(false)≅F_k(true) whose conjugated hom is e.hom. Moreover, if p:G(A)≅T, q:G(B)≅T and e:A≅B satisfy p.inv≫G(e.hom)≫q.hom=id_T, then p=G(e)≫q as isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 09RE, lemma-descend-homomorphisms; Tag 09RF, fully faithful overlap descent before gluing

proof.text: Lift e.hom and e.inv separately and transport them to a common upper bound. Transport preserves their limit images. Functoriality and cancellation of ψ show that the two stage composites have limit images equal to the corresponding identity maps.

Apply eventual Hom equality to both composites. Choose a common upper bound of the two equality stages. Identity and composition preservation turn the two stabilized relations into inverse equations for the transported maps. Form their isomorphism and retain its prescribed hom image.
For the comparison assertion, take homs and cancel p.inv on the left; p.inv≫p.hom=id and the assumed conjugated identity give the claimed equation.

lean.statement:
theorem DirectedPerfectHomSystem.lift_iso
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    {C : I → Type v} [∀ k, Category.{h} (C k)]
    {F : ∀ k, Bool → C k} {D : Type v'} [Category.{h'} D]
    {O : Bool → D} {G : ∀ k, C k ⥤ D}
    {ψ : ∀ k b, (G k).obj (F k b) ≅ O b}
    (H : DirectedPerfectHomSystem I C F D O G ψ) (e : O false ≅ O true) :
    ∃ (k : I) (ek : F k false ≅ F k true),
      (ψ k false).inv ≫ (G k).map ek.hom ≫ (ψ k true).hom = e.hom
